about: Lesson L12, the training loop. Computed by tools/school/fill_trainloop.mjs from system/school/trainloop.mjs and the attention lab's own trainer. Do not edit by hand. Losses are in nats (natural log).

recipe.about: What the lab's trainer does each step, read off the code. Batch: 16 rows of 24 words cut from a seeded stream of whole corpus episodes. Forward, then mean cross-entropy over all 384 next-word targets. Backward: a hand-written gradient for every parameter (checked against finite differences in the tinyformer tests). Clip: if the global L2 norm of the whole gradient exceeds 1.0, every gradient is scaled by 1.0 / norm. Step: Adam (Kingma and Ba 2015, arXiv 1412.6980, Algorithm 1: bias-corrected first and second moment estimates) with beta1 0.9, beta2 0.99 (the paper's suggested default is 0.999), epsilon 1e-8, and decoupled weight decay 0.01 as in AdamW (Loshchilov and Hutter 2019, arXiv 1711.05101), applied to weight matrices and embeddings only, never to gains or biases. One difference from the paper's Algorithm 2: there the decay term is scaled by the schedule multiplier only; here it is scaled by the full learning rate (the convention of common libraries), so the per-step shrink is lr x 0.01. Learning rate: linear warmup from lr/30 to lr over the first 30 steps, then constant; no decay schedule.

reproduce.about: Re-trained from the model's seeds (model seed 7, data seed 11) with the lab's own trainer for the full 2000 steps, scored every 25 steps on the same 256 held-out rows, and compared with the curve stored in model.json after rounding to 4 decimals. tensorsEqual: weight tensors whose float32 bytes match model.json exactly. gradNormsEqual: logged gradient norms (every 25 steps) equal after rounding. Bit-identical on this engine (V8 in Node); the code notes another engine may differ in the last bit of exp and tanh and drift from there, which this run does not test.

gradients.about: The global L2 norm of the gradient at every one of the 2000 steps of the reproduced run, measured before clipping. clipped: steps where the norm exceeded 1, so the clip scaled the step down. byWindow: the same per block of 250 steps. One run: how often the clip fires depends on the seed, the batch size and the learning rate.

variants.about: One change each from the reference recipe (batch 16, lr 0.01 with 30 warmup steps, clip 1, weight decay 0.01, data seed 11, model seed 7), trained 1000 steps where not stated and scored every 50 steps on the same 256 held-out rows. reference is the reproduced run's first 1000 steps. Batch runs: batch4Steps keeps the step count (a quarter of the words); batch4Tokens and batch64Tokens keep the words seen (384000 target words) and so change the step count; the learning rate is not rescaled with batch size. noise: the reference recipe with data seeds 12 and 13, to show how far two runs that differ only in luck land apart; a variant inside that spread is not shown to differ. firstCopyStep: first scored step with copy accuracy at or above 0.9 (null: never in this run). One seed per variant: a single run each, so differences smaller than the noise runs' spread are not evidence.

controls.about: Two broken loops that must fail to learn, from the same seeds, 200 steps each. lrZero: learning rate 0, so every update is zero and the held-out loss must stay at its starting value. uphill: the gradient's sign flipped before the optimiser, so each step climbs the loss. startLoss is the untrained network's held-out loss on the same rows. A control that fails shows the measurement can tell learning from not learning; it does not show the normal recipe is the best one.

speed.about: Time per training step in Node (V8, one thread, float32 buffers), measured alone after the training runs finished: anatomy times 60 steps split into drawing the batch, a forward pass, forward plus backward, and the optimiser update. tokensPerSecond counts target words per second of a full step. reproduceMsPerStep is the wall time per step of the reproduced run, which shared the machine with up to 3 other runs. One machine and one engine: a browser tab or another CPU will differ.
